name: IFEval (Instruction-Following Evaluation)
description: A benchmark dataset for evaluating the instruction-following ability of Large Language Models (LLMs) using verifiable instructions. The dataset contains 541 prompts with 25 types of verifiable instructions such as word count constraints, formatting requirements, keyword inclusion, and language specifications.

creator.name: Jeffrey Zhou, Tianjian Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Siddhartha Brahma, Sujoy Basu, Yi Luan, Denny Zhou, Le Hou

citeAs: Jeffrey Zhou, Tianjian Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Siddhartha Brahma, Sujoy Basu, Yi Luan, Denny Zhou, Le Hou. Instruction-Following Evaluation for Large Language Models. arXiv:2311.07911v1 [cs.CL] 14 Nov 2023
rai:dataCollection: Prompts were generated through a four-step process: (1) generating base prompts with one to three randomly selected verifiable instructions appended, (2) using few-shot prompting to identify and remove illogical prompts, (3) applying few-shot prompting to rephrase each prompt for diversity, and (4) manually checking and editing the rephrased prompts one by one.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Base prompts were generated with randomly selected verifiable instructions from a list of 25 instruction types. The instructions include constraints on keywords, language, length, format, content, and other verifiable aspects.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Few-shot prompting was used to identify illogical prompts and remove them. Another few-shot prompting approach was applied to rephrase each prompt to increase diversity of phrasing.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Manual curation was performed to check and edit rephrased prompts one by one. Transformations were applied to responses during evaluation including: removing markdown font modifiers, removing first/last lines, and combinations of these transformations.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Verification of instruction-following is performed programmatically using deterministic heuristics. Each verifiable instruction has a corresponding verification function that checks if the response follows the instruction. A loose verification criterion is also implemented that applies multiple transformations to reduce false negatives.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Two accuracy metrics are computed: strict-accuracy (using exact verification) and loose-accuracy (using transformations to reduce false negatives). Both prompt-level and instruction-level accuracies are calculated. The loose criterion may introduce false positives while reducing false negatives.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark aims to provide an objective, reproducible, and unbiased method for evaluating instruction-following capabilities of LLMs, which is crucial for safety and reliability of LLM implementations, especially in critical scenarios like healthcare or autonomous systems.
rai:dataLimitations: While the focus is on verifiable instructions, very few instructions are 100% verifiable objectively and automatically - edge cases exist where it is hard to determine if an instruction is followed. The verification approach attempts to handle common variations but may still produce false negatives or false positives. The current implementation focuses on text-based instructions and does not cover multi-modal use cases.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for evaluating the instruction-following ability of Large Language Models. It provides baseline evaluation results for GPT-4 and PaLM 2 models. Researchers can use the benchmark to analyze what types of instructions are not usually followed and compare different LLMs on various instruction types.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Few-shot prompting was used for identifying illogical prompts and rephrasing prompts. Programmatic verification functions were implemented to check instruction-following.
